the short answer

The agencies that handle founder LinkedIn content end to end in 2026 include rallyup, Windmill Growth and Kurogo, with CSuite Content for CEOs who also want PR. rallyup is the strongest fit for B2B founders and leadership teams who want a dedicated human writer per executive, every post approved in Slack, publishing, a profile rewrite, ICP connection requests and a monthly report under one price, from $5,000 per executive per month, with a guarantee of 100k organic impressions in 90 days or you don't pay. Windmill Growth suits a single founder who wants outbound and inbox management bundled in ($3,999 a month for Founder OS), and Kurogo suits UK executives who want carousels and graphics as standard (from £1,500 a month). If you only need polish on posts you write yourself, an editor or freelancer is the better buy.

rallyup publishes this page and is one of the services compared, so weigh the sections on other providers with that in mind.

what "end to end" should actually include

Many services call themselves done-for-you and then hand you drafts. Writing is one step of eight. If any of the others sits with you, the work is shared, and in our experience the part that sits with a busy founder is the part that stops first.

  • Strategy. Who the posts are for, what you want to be known for, and a weekly plan of topics.
  • Interviews. A set rhythm of conversations that pulls stories and opinions out of you, so posts don't run dry after a month.
  • Writing. Posts in your voice, by a writer who stays with you.
  • Approvals. A simple way to approve, edit or reject every post before it goes live.
  • Publishing. Someone schedules and posts for you, at the times your audience is online.
  • Profile. An About section and Featured links that turn a curious visitor into a conversation.
  • Audience. Connection requests to the buyers you want reading, so reach grows among the right people.
  • Reporting. A monthly view of impressions, followers, profile views, connections and inbound messages.

who handles it, and who each one fits

rallyup: founders and leadership teams

rallyup is a done-for-you LinkedIn ghostwriting agency for B2B founders and executives. Each executive gets a dedicated human writer, three posts a week published at peak times, a story interview twice a month, a profile rewrite, automated ICP connection requests and a monthly progress report, with every post approved in Slack first. Most clients start with one executive and then roll it out to the wider leadership team.

Across the executives in our executive linkedin benchmarks 2026, monthly impressions grew a median 4.7x in the first 90 days compared with the 90 days before (7 executives with complete account data), and followers grew a median 17.4% in about 90 days (9 executives). Named results are on our case studies page, including an Airwallex program that reached 701,198 impressions across 39 posts in two and a half months, and a PandaDoc program where three executives produced 1,235 engagements in one month.

Windmill Growth: a single founder who wants outbound too

A New York agency for B2B founders. Founder OS includes a weekly 30-minute interview, up to five posts a week shared across LinkedIn and X, brand strategy, a profile rebuild, ICP outreach and inbox management. Windmill says it takes three new clients a month and only accepts founders in industries where it already has expertise.

Kurogo: UK executives who want design and PR

A London personal branding agency. Its ghostwriting plans include 10 to 20 posts a month with carousels and graphics as standard, scheduling and a monthly report, and it also offers PR and lead generation.

CSuite Content: CEOs who want PR alongside posts

Combines LinkedIn ghostwriting (about 8 to 10 posts a month) with op-eds, speeches and earned media. Pricing is quoted per client, and it says engagements typically start at six months.

outbound-first agencies: when booked meetings come first

Media Engine bundles ghostwriting with outreach, commenting and appointment setting. SalesBread started as a LinkedIn outreach agency and added ghostwriting. Both fit teams where outbound is the main motion and content supports it. For more providers and their published prices, see the linkedin ghostwriting agencies comparison.

how to vet a done-for-you service

  • Walk the eight steps with them. For each one, ask who does it and what you do. Anything that lands on your side is work you are still doing.
  • Ask who writes, and whether it stays the same person. Voice depends on continuity, and on regular interviews rather than a single questionnaire.
  • Ask about AI. rallyup uses human writers and keeps AI to research. Whatever the answer, it should be clear.
  • Ask what cadence they hold. In our benchmark, the bigger gains came from consistency (a median 22 to 31 posts per 90 days) and breakout posts: the top 10% of posts produced 75% of impressions.
  • Ask for a sample report. Impressions alone are not enough. Look for profile views, ICP connections and inbound messages. As a reference point, the median engagement rate per post in our benchmark was 2.18% (453 posts).
  • Ask for results from someone like you. Named companies and real numbers, not only testimonials.
  • Check the terms. Minimum contract length, what happens if a post doesn't sound like you, and whether there is any guarantee.

Still deciding between a single writer and a full service? Our guide to linkedin ghostwriter vs agency covers the trade-offs, and how long linkedin ghostwriting takes to work sets out a realistic 90-day timeline.

when rallyup isn't the right fit

  • Your budget is under $5,000 a month per executive.
  • You want to write it yourself and just need editing.
  • You need meetings in the next 30 days rather than an audience that produces them over a quarter. An outbound-first agency fits better.
  • Your goals are B2C or creator growth. We write for B2B founders and executives selling to other businesses.
  • You can't give a 30-minute story interview twice a month. That conversation is where the posts come from.
